title: Do plants breathe?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Do plants give out carbon dioxide at night?

explain.say: Plants do breathe, in their own way. Every living plant cell needs energy and gets it by respiration, just as we do. But plants also do photosynthesis, which swaps the same gases the other way.
In light, leaves do photosynthesis: they take in carbon dioxide, build sugar and give out oxygen. On a bright day this runs much faster than respiration, so leaves give out more oxygen than they use.
Respiration happens all day and all night, in roots, stems, leaves and flowers. Cells use oxygen to break down sugar for energy, giving out carbon dioxide and water.
Plants have no lungs. Air simply drifts in through stomata on leaves and tiny pores on stems and roots, spreads through air spaces, and every cell takes the oxygen it needs.

stages.label: Energy released
stages.note: Sugar is broken down for energy

stages.label: Carbon dioxide out
stages.note: Waste gas drifts out or is reused

faq.a: Yes. Plants respire day and night, taking in oxygen and giving out carbon dioxide. At night, with no light for photosynthesis, they only give out carbon dioxide, but far less than a person does.
asks: Is it bad to have plants in a bedroom?

faq.q: What is the difference between photosynthesis and respiration?
faq.a: Photosynthesis uses light to build sugar from carbon dioxide and water, giving out oxygen. Respiration breaks sugar down to release energy, using oxygen and giving out carbon dioxide. They are nearly opposites.

No. Gases move in and out by diffusion through stomata on leaves, small pores called lenticels on stems, and the surface of roots. Plants need far less oxygen than animals, so they manage without lungs.
Root cells respire too, so they need oxygen from air spaces in the soil. That is why most plants die if their soil stays waterlogged for too long.

faq.q: Do plants make more oxygen than they use?
faq.a: Over a whole day, a healthy growing plant makes more oxygen by photosynthesis than it uses in respiration. The extra is what fills our air.

facts: Plants respire all the time, day and night, in every living cell.
Woody stems exchange gases through small pores called lenticels.
Waterlogged soil can suffocate roots because water fills the air spaces they need.

quiz.say: Which gas does a plant give out in complete darkness?
quiz.show: Which gas does a plant give out in complete darkness?
quiz.why: In the dark there is no photosynthesis, but respiration carries on and releases carbon dioxide.

wrong.1: Oxygen is given out by photosynthesis, which needs light.
wrong.2: Respiration never stops, so some gas is always exchanged.
